instructions: SECTION 4 · You will hear part of a lecture about bioluminescence.

groups.instructions: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
groups.strategy: Section 4 is a monologue with no break. Use the headings in the notes as signposts — the lecturer will say 'Now, where…', 'So what is it used for?' Answers are usually nouns. Check spelling and singular/plural.

questions.prompt: Chemistry: luciferin reacts with ________ with the help of the enzyme luciferase.
questions.explanation: 'When luciferin reacts with oxygen, with the help of luciferase'.

questions.prompt: Called 'cold light' because very little ________ is produced.
questions.explanation: 'almost no heat is produced at all'.

questions.prompt: Deep sea off California: about three-quarters of ________ observed produced light.
questions.explanation: 'roughly three-quarters of the animals observed'. Plural needed.

questions.prompt: Most marine light is blue or green because these colours travel furthest through ________.
Finding food: the anglerfish uses a glowing ________ to attract prey.
questions.explanation: 'a glowing lure that hangs in front of its mouth'.

questions.prompt: Defence — counter-illumination hides an animal's ________ from predators below.
Communication: each firefly species has its own ________ of flashes.
questions.explanation: 'each species has its own pattern of flashes'.

questions.prompt: Bobtail squid: gives its bacteria ________ and a safe home.
questions.explanation: 'The squid provides the bacteria with sugar and a safe place to live'.

questions.prompt: GFP was first found in a ________.
questions.explanation: 'researchers studying a jellyfish discovered a protein'.

questions.prompt: Glowing bacteria are used to detect ________ in water.
questions.explanation: 'glowing bacteria are already used in tests for water pollution'.
